root_cause.text: The qla2xxx driver allowed module unload to proceed while a fabric scan was still in progress, causing DMA memory to be freed in interrupt context (via `dma_free_attrs` in `qla24xx_sp_unmap`) when a scan completion interrupt was handled after the UNLOADING flag was set, because the work item allocation was skipped.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "The root cause of this was that there was a free (dma_free_attrs) in the interrupt context. There was a device discovery/fabric scan in progress. A module unload was issued which set the UNLOADING flag. As part of the discovery, after receiving an interrupt a work queue was scheduled (which involved a work to be queued). Since the UNLOADING flag is set, the work item was not allocated and the mapped memory had to be freed. The free occurred in interrupt context leading to system crash." The patch adds a wait condition `(vha->scan.scan_flags & SF_SCANNING)` in `qla2x00_wait_for_hba_ready()` to delay module unload until the fabric scan completes.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix missing wait for ongoing scan by adding SF_SCANNING flag check in qla2x00_wait_for_hba_ready loop.
intent_record.what: Added an additional condition to the while loop in qla2x00_wait_for_hba_ready: (vha->scan.scan_flags & SF_SCANNING).
intent_record.how: The loop now continues to wait (sleep 1000ms) as long as the scan scanning flag is set, in addition to the existing conditions (reset active, dpc active, mbox busy, FX00_RESET_RECOVERY, FX00_TARGET_SCAN). This prevents the function from returning prematurely while a scan is in progress.

grouping_result.intent: Fix missing wait for ongoing scan by adding SF_SCANNING flag check in qla2x00_wait_for_hba_ready loop.

relevance_review.reason: The group adds a check for the SF_SCANNING flag in a wait loop, which directly addresses the root cause of not waiting for an ongoing fabric scan before module unload.

candidates.rationale: When the UNLOADING flag is set, this break immediately exits the waiting loop without checking whether a fabric scan is still in progress. This allows module unload to proceed while a scan completion interrupt may still free DMA memory, leading to use-after-free.
This condition triggers the premature exit from the wait loop. It permits the unload path to skip waiting for an ongoing fabric scan, which is the root cause of the vulnerability.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition allows the wait loop to exit when the UNLOADING flag is set, without checking if a fabric scan is still in progress. This permits module unload to proceed while a scan completion interrupt may still free DMA memory, leading to use-after-free.

Executing this break immediately exits the wait loop when the UNLOADING flag is set, skipping the wait for an ongoing fabric scan. This allows DMA memory to be freed in interrupt context after the module unload has started, causing a use-after-free vulnerability.
